fit: open-label amantadine and ever-reported adverse events
assessment: EASE LID 2 follows 223 participants receiving open-label extended-release amantadine for Parkinson dyskinesia. Hallucination adverse events and time to onset were tracked; the common named event was reported in 24.2% of participants. The extension re-enrolled participants from earlier trials and also enrolled a deep-brain-stimulation cohort. NCT02202551 is a medication safety study without a dried fig exposure or controlled food comparison.

fit: subthalamic stimulation and a nighttime distress item
assessment: A Parkinson cohort was followed after bilateral subthalamic stimulation. The sleep scale includes an item for distressing nighttime hallucinations, which differs from all-day visual episode counts. Stimulation follow-up and medication context provide no comparison by dried fig intake.

fit: open-label opicapone and serious adverse-event context
assessment: OPTIPARK is an open-label opicapone safety and effectiveness study for motor fluctuations. Visual hallucination appears among serious events considered possibly treatment related. Seven of 495 participants had one or more of the listed related serious events, a grouped figure that cannot be assigned to visual hallucination alone. The study intervention was opicapone and there is no dried fig exposure.

fit: Parkinson cohort protocol with dietary diaries and nonmotor phenotyping
assessment: DUPARC specifies vision and other nonmotor phenotyping in de novo Parkinson disease and planned a three-day dietary diary for nutrient intake. It also identifies diet as a potential confounder in the microbiome analysis. The protocol reports no separate dried fig measure, fig comparison or exposure-linked visual hallucination outcome. Registry NCT04180865 identifies this cohort.

fit: care partner interviews about hallucination modality and experience
assessment: The qualitative study interviewed care partners about lived experience of Parkinson psychosis and reports multiple hallucination modalities. The interview data provide symptom and caregiving context. They supply neither a dried fig comparison nor a prospective count of visual episodes by diet.

fit: randomized amantadine and pooled hallucinations and psychosis item
assessment: The pooled post hoc analysis uses EASE LID and EASE LID 3 data, NCT02136914 and NCT02274766. At week 12 the MDS-UPDRS hallucinations and psychosis item was 0.2 points higher after Gocovri than after placebo in the adjusted analysis (P < 0.001). The scored item combines experiences and cannot be treated as an independent food effect or a count of visual episodes. This analysis overlaps the parent randomized trial populations, which also contributed extension participants.

fit: visual frequency and severity at baseline and later cognition
assessment: A prospective Parkinson analysis evaluates baseline visual hallucinations and subjective cognitive complaints as predictors of later cognition. The NMSS perception domain records frequency and severity over the prior four weeks. The modeled outcome is cognitive impairment during follow-up and the study does not compare dried fig intake.

fit: retrospective exposure to identified Annonaceae plants and composite parkinsonism severity
assessment: Visual hallucination presence is 18.00% in the milder profile and 46.75% in the severe profile. Adjusted dietary results give odds of composite-profile membership by fruit, juice or herbal tea exposure. The study does not estimate visual episode frequency given an exposure, and the plant family differs from common fig.

fit: Parkinson questionnaire with separate visual and nonvisual experiences
assessment: The 369-person survey measures unusual sensory experience over the preceding month. It reports item frequency and pooled experience and distress measures without a documented dried fig or dietary trigger analysis.

fit: inspected historical edition separates heavy fresh intake and dried storage
assessment: The written account attaches excitement to heavy fresh fruit consumption during the harvest. Sun-dried figs and some dipped in oil are described separately, with no comparable reported experience. The literary account gives no clinical visual hallucination or Parkinson outcome.
